'''Laura Cadonati''' is an American [[physicist]] who specializes in [[gravitational waves]].

==Career==
Cadonati completed her PhD at [[Princeton University]] in 2001 with her thesis ''The Borexino Solar Neutrino Experiment and its Scintillator Containment Vessel''. She was an associate professor in the physics department at [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]] before moving to the Center for Relativistic Astrophysics at [[Georgia Institute of Technology]] in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physics.umass.edu/people/laura-cadonati|title=Laura Cadonati &#124; Department of Physics &#124; UMass Amherst|website=Physics Department at UMass Amherst}}</ref>

Cadonati has been a member of the [[LIGO|Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory]] (LIGO) collaboration since 2002,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cadonati.gatech.edu/|title=Laura Cadonati – Laura Cadonati – Gravitational Wave Astrophysics @ Georgia Tech|website=cadonati.gatech.edu}}</ref> and was involved in the first observations of gravitational waves in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.gatech.edu/archive/features/gravitational-waves-observed.shtml|title=Gravitational Waves Observed|website=news.gatech.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.atlantamagazine.com/news-culture-articles/georgia-tech-physicists-helped-prove-einstein-right/|title=These Georgia Tech physicists helped prove Einstein right|first=Myrydd|last=Wells|date=September 19, 2016}}</ref>

In 2017 she became the first deputy spokesperson for LIGO<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.gatech.edu/news/2017/04/20/college-sciences-professor-appointed-top-role-search-gravitational-waves|title=College of Sciences Professor Appointed to Top Role in Search for Gravitational Waves &#124; News Center|website=news.gatech.edu}}</ref> and was widely quoted in the media as LIGO detected its third gravitational wave.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.gatech.edu/news/2017/10/16/scientists-make-first-detection-neutron-star-collision|title=Scientists Make First Detection of Neutron Star Collision &#124; News Center|website=news.gatech.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scienceandcocktails.org/en/events/brussels/seeing-with-new-eyes-gravitational-waves|title=Seeing with new eyes: Gravitational waves &#124; Science and Cocktails|website=www.scienceandcocktails.org|date=7 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.sky.com/story/scientists-discover-incredible-origin-of-gold-to-herald-new-chapter-in-astrophysics-11083888|title=Scientists discover incredible origin of gold to herald 'new chapter in astrophysics'|website=Sky News|date=17 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/gravitational-wave-astronomers-hit-mother-lode1/|title=Gravitational Wave Astronomers Hit Mother Lode|first=Lee|last=Billings|website=Scientific American|date=16 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.co.uk/article/gravitational-waves-found-third-time|title=They've done it again! Ligo scientists find gravitational waves for the third time|magazine=Wired |via=www.wired.co.uk|date=1 June 2017 |last1=Burgess |first1=Matt }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.theguardian.com/science/2017/jun/01/third-gravitational-wave-detection-gives-hints-on-dark-matter-and-black-holes|title=Third gravitational wave detection gives hints on dark matter and black holes|date=June 1, 2017|work=The Guardian|author=Hannah Devlin}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-40120680|title=Gravitational waves: Third detection of deep space warping|date=June 1, 2017|via=www.bbc.co.uk|author=Jonathan Amos}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://astronomynow.com/2017/06/03/black-holes-crash-together-and-make-waves/|title=Black holes crash together and make waves – Astronomy Now|date=3 June 2017|author=William Harwood}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/science/article/black-holes-gravitational-waves-space-genius-science|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211004035735/https://www.nationalgeographic.com/science/article/black-holes-gravitational-waves-space-genius-science|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 4, 2021|title=Bizarre Black Holes Revealed by New Space-Time Ripples|date=June 1, 2017|website=Science|author=Nadia Drake}}</ref>{{overcite|date=October 2024}}

Cadonati became associate dean for research in the College of Sciences at Georgia Institute of Technology in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chemistry.gatech.edu/index.php/news/laura-cadonati-named-associate-dean-research|title=Laura Cadonati Named Associate Dean for Research &#124; School of Chemistry & Biochemistry|website=chemistry.gatech.edu|date=8 July 2021}}</ref>

She is a member of the [[International Astronomical Union]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iau.org/administration/membership/individual/16129/|title=International Astronomical Union &#124; IAU|website=www.iau.org}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* 2010: [[National Science Foundation]] CAREER award<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physics.umass.edu/news/2010-10-01-cadonati-wins-nsf-career-grant|title=Cadonati wins NSF Career grant &#124; Department of Physics &#124; UMass Amherst|website=Physics Department at UMass Amherst|date=1 October 2010}}</ref>
* 2015: [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] for "leadership of the gravitational-wave data analysis and astrophysics efforts of the LIGO Scientific Collaboration, including work connecting numerical modeling of sources to observations with the LIGO, Virgo, and GEO detectors"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org}}</ref>
* 2018: Outstanding Faculty Research Author Award<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cos.gatech.edu/news/laura-cadonati-2018-outstanding-faculty-research-author-award|title=Laura Cadonati: 2018 Outstanding Faculty Research Author Award &#124; College of Sciences &#124; Georgia Institute of Technology &#124; Atlanta, GA|website=cos.gatech.edu|date=2 April 2018}}</ref>
